messages.author: bd20e150e28c63db
messages.subject: coverage filtering with destrand=TRUE
parts:
Hello,

I use methylkit for rrbs data.

I kept only bases with coverage>5. I then used the destrand=TRUE option when uniting the samples. I think that this is not good.
When using destrand - would you suggest to do the filtering after the unite - let's say to keep only CpGs that had a total of 5 reads (on either strand)?  (Unfortunately my coverage is very low).
Any suggestion when and how it is the best to do the coverage filtering when destrand=TRUE?

Thanks

messages.author: e4181d5c40fc094c
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] coverage filtering with destrand=TRUE
parts:
Hi,

Filtering the bases before performing 'unite' may not give desired results in this case.

In cases of low coverage, the following sequence of steps may be of some help:
  • Read every CpG (no coverage cutoff)
  • Remove CpG with extremely high coverage using 'normalizeCoverage'
  • Perform 'unite' (destrand=T)
  • Filter CpGs with a given threshold across all the samples

Hope this helps!


Regards,
Kalyan

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] coverage filtering with destrand=TRUE
parts:
To my understanding, 'tileMethylCounts' function can use any of the methylRaw, methylRawList or methylBase objects. So, I would proceed by filtering the methylBase object (coverage>threshold) followed by 'tileMethylCounts'.

I am not sure if one can combine the strand coverage while generating methylRaw or methylRawList objects. This leaves me with the only option to compute tiling only on methylBase object.

Regards,
Kalyan
